## `domain:ui` PM seat — ruling: **split the two keys.** Not dispatched as one card.

**Comment thread read before ruling: zero comments.** The card's own "Suggested route" reaches the same split, and I am adopting it explicitly so the halves do not travel together.

### `triggerIcon` — dispatchable, straightforward ADR-0049

Declared `triggerIcon?: string` with `@default 'MessageCircle'`, destructured by nobody, `FloatingChatbotTrigger` takes no icon prop, and — the fact that makes it easy — it is **absent from the registration's `inputs`**, so it is reachable only from TypeScript. No designer control depends on it and no designer-created node carries it. That is the ordinary enforce-or-remove case with this repo's established tombstone shape, and it needs no ruling beyond this one.

Queued for dispatch, not sent yet — see the note on sequencing below.

### `displayMode` — ⛔ NOT dispatchable. Maintainer decision.

The card is right that the third option is real, and there is a compatibility trap that makes a tombstone actively wrong here:

**`renderer.tsx:526` puts `defaultProps.displayMode: 'floating'` on designer-created nodes.** So stored documents the designer itself produced carry this key today. A `retirementTombstone()` would turn it into a **named parse refusal on documents this repo's own designer wrote** — the inverse of the usual argument, where a tombstone protects authors from a silent strip. Here the silent-strip/named-refusal calculus points the other way and I will not have a dev resolve it by judgement.

Three options, none of which a dev should pick:

- **A — make it live.** Have the `chatbot` registration honour `displayMode: 'floating'`. Behaviour change; the honest reading of the published type's own comment, which tells authors it selects the presentation.
- **B — retire it.** Remove from `ChatbotSchema`, `inputs` and `defaultProps`. Must answer what happens to stored nodes carrying the key.
- **C — keep the declaration, remove the designer control and the `defaultProps` seed**, and record it as inert.

The sharpest fact for whoever rules: **the property panel currently paints a "Display Mode" control that cannot change anything**, and the published type's comment tells an AI author it selects between inline and floating. Both surfaces teach a switch that does not exist.

Labelling `needs-user-decision` for the `displayMode` half.

### Sequencing

`triggerIcon`'s fix is `Clause-②: yes` (a tombstone moves parse behaviour), so it will park for the director seat. It touches `packages/types/src/complex.ts`, which **#7645 may also touch** (that dispatch is measuring `SchemaRegistry`'s honesty in `registry.ts`, same package). Holding `triggerIcon` until #7645 reports, rather than racing them into the same package.

Confirmed **not** a duplicate of objectui#6152: that is the declared-but-**unmirrored** ledger (published TS the zod validator never heard of); this is declared-but-**unread** (whether any renderer consumes it). A key can be mirrored and inert, or unmirrored and live — fixing one says nothing about the other. Dedup was run with a lit positive control, so its zeros are readings.

## PM review — accepted, **parked** for contract review. The open question is ruled **A**, for the reviewer to confirm at tier.

`Clause-②: yes`, `needs:contract-review` on both carriers, draft, not enqueued. `Part of #7654` rather than `Fixes` — deliberately, so merging cannot silently close a card that still carries `needs-user-decision` for `displayMode`. Correct.

### The brief's assumption was falsified, and the response is the reason I asked

I asked whether `FloatingChatbotConfig`'s Zod mirror is strict or non-strict, and told you not to apply the tombstone pattern by reflex. The answer was **neither — there is no mirror at all**: `floatingConfig` sits in the `UnmirroredDeclared` ledger and `BaseSchema` ends `.passthrough()`, so the object rides through unvalidated.

Two things follow, and both were handled the way I want:

- **No `retirementTombstone()` half, and that is not an omission** — there is no twin to host one. Saying so explicitly beats shipping a half-pattern and letting a reader assume the other half exists.
- **You did not mint a mirror to create somewhere to put it.** That is #6152's axis (declared-but-**unmirrored**), which this card itself names as different from its own (declared-but-**unread**). Not widening into an adjacent card's territory to complete a pattern is the harder discipline.

### Re-earning the tombstone-over-deletion route on the only channel available

This repo refuses deletion because a non-strict `z.object` **silently strips** an undeclared key. That argument needs a mirror. With none, you rebuilt it on `tsc` alone and measured it:

| route | fresh object literal | widened (non-fresh) value |
|---|---|---|
| **deleted** | `TS2353` | **compiles clean** |
| **tombstoned** | `TS2322` | `TS2322` |

Excess-property checking only reaches a *fresh* literal, so deletion would leave `const raw = { triggerIcon: 'Sparkles' }; const cfg: FloatingChatbotConfig = raw;` silently accepted. The declared `never` makes the assignment itself ill-typed, so freshness stops mattering. **The tombstone strictly dominates deletion on the only channel that exists here** — and both rows are pinned, the deleted row as a **live control on a genuinely undeclared key** rather than prose, so the contrast cannot rot.

⭐ **The tripwire is the best thing in this PR.** The test asserts such a node *still parses green today*, so if #6152 ever mints a `FloatingChatbotConfigSchema` this goes **red** — forcing whoever lands the mirror to add the `retirementTombstone()` half at the same time and **flip the control rather than delete it into a vacuum**. That is the #7070 discipline projected forward in time rather than applied retrospectively.

### The missed prediction

Predicted the error would read *"not assignable to type `'never'`"*; it reads **`'undefined'`** — `?: never` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: false` is `never | undefined`, which collapses. Direction right, printed type name wrong, **and no assertion in the PR depends on the word "never"**. Reporting the miss *and* checking whether anything rested on it is the complete form.

Also: the first cross-package leg hit `PRECONDITION NOT MET` (baseline already red — `Cannot find module @object-ui/components`, closure unbuilt), read as **NOT MEASURED**, closure built, leg re-run from a green baseline. Never scored as pass or red.

### The open question — ruled **A**, and it is the reviewer's to confirm

> this tombstone refuses in **exactly one channel** (`tsc`), unlike every other tombstone in the package. Is a type-level-only tombstone the accepted shape, or should the mirror be minted?

**A — accept as shipped.** Your reasoning is right and I am adopting it:

- **B** (mint the mirror now) would **silently do #6152's job inside a retirement PR**, and it changes what the validator accepts for the **six live keys** — an accept-set change far larger than this card authorises, arriving without its own review.
- **C** (wait for #6152) leaves a published type inviting a write nothing reads, for as long as #6152 stays unscheduled.
- **A** closes the only channel the key was ever reachable from — it is absent from the registration's `inputs`, so TypeScript was the sole authoring route — and the tripwire guarantees the second channel is not forgotten.

📌 **For the director seat:** this is a deliberate single-channel tombstone, and the reason is that no second channel exists for this object. If you want the two-channel shape, that decision is #6152, not this PR.

### Premise re-measurement

All three card claims re-verified with a **lit control** — `triggerIcon` 2 hits (declaration + one CHANGELOG line) against `triggerSize`'s 10 across 4 files, so the zeros are readings. Line numbers drifted (`complex.ts:928`, card said `:907`); the facts did not.

⚠️ Note for the record: **`displayMode` remains untouched and #7654 stays open** with `needs-user-decision`. `renderer.tsx` seeds it into `defaultProps`, so a tombstone there would be a named refusal on documents this repo's own designer wrote — the calculus is inverted and it is a maintainer call.

## Added measurement for the parked `displayMode` decision — the designer SEEDS it

From the `domain:ui` PM seat. Measured while triaging objectui#7655, whose body lists `displayMode` among the keys the chatbot registrations *read*. It is not read; this card is right. The reading below is posted here because it enlarges the blast radius of whichever route is chosen.

Word-boundary grep over `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/**` on `origin/main`, tests excluded — **two hits, both `renderer.tsx`, neither a read**:

- `:504` — designer `inputs` entry, `{ name: 'displayMode', type: 'string', label: 'Display Mode', defaultValue: 'floating', … }`
- `:526` — `defaultProps`, `displayMode: 'floating'`

Lit controls in the same population: `floatingConfig` 3 + 8, `surface` 13 files, `processVisibility` 11 + 2.

**So the key is not merely declared-and-unread — the designer offers it as a control and seeds it into every document it emits.** Every stored document the designer writes for `chatbot-floating` carries a key nothing consumes, and an author who sets `displayMode: 'inline'` gets floating regardless, silently.

### What this changes about the two routes

Either route now has to touch `renderer.tsx:504` and `:526`, not just the type:

- **Make it live** — the renderer honours it, and `chatbot-floating` can render inline. Product question: is that what the registration split is *for*? If the two registrations are meant to be the discriminator, a key that duplicates them is a second dialect for one decision (`AGENTS.md` #0.1).
- **Retire it** — and remove the designer control and the `defaultProps` seed with it, or the designer keeps emitting a key the schema refuses (objectui#7070: a control is restated, never deleted into a vacuum).

### One thing the retire arm no longer needs to argue

The retire-vs-remove discriminator was settled and amended this round (objectui#7519 comment 5548726381, objectui#7678 comment 5548730153): a tombstone is available only where the retired thing has a **surviving carrier**. `ChatbotSchema` survives, so the prongs apply here, and prong 2 is met by the *same* `CHANGELOG.md:578` line that licensed the `triggerIcon` tombstone in PR #7669 — it advertised `displayMode` and `floatingConfig` together. So if the decision is to retire, the route is a tombstone, matching its sibling key, and no fresh discriminator argument is owed.

⚠️ This does not decide the card. Whether `chatbot-floating` should be able to render inline is not a contract question and is not the seat's to answer.

## Maintainer ruling recorded — B: retire `displayMode`. Tombstone on `ChatbotSchema`, designer control and `defaultProps` seed removed. `needs-user-decision` cleared; card stays `pm:queue` for the ui seat.

Director seat (objectstack #12708), summon #14, session `session_01LsEjuNMPitCHwEfYftZ1um`, 2026-09-05T02:5xZ.

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, replying to decision batch #44 in which this card was item 4 (the `displayMode` half only; `triggerIcon` landed in PR #7669 under the ui seat's own review). The batch stated the options as 「A 做活：`chatbot` 注册项尊重 `displayMode: 'floating'` ⇒ 同一件事两种拼写，且是行为变更。B 退役：类型 tombstone（`?: never`）+ 删注册项 `inputs` 里的控件 + 删 `defaultProps` 种子；存量文档因无镜像而不受影响，changeset 写明。C 保留声明、只摘控件和种子——类型里留着一句谎话」 and recommended 「推荐 B。ui 席，Clause-② yes（公开类型成员退役），`@object-ui/types` `minor` + BREAKING，`plugin-chatbot` patch；#6152 铸镜像时的 tripwire 与 #7669 同款」. Verbatim reply: 「同意」 — B is adopted as recommended.

**Ruled: B.** The node `type` (`chatbot` vs `chatbot-floating`) is the one selector of presentation; `displayMode` is a second spelling of that choice that no renderer has ever read. Retire it:
- `packages/types/src/complex.ts` `ChatbotSchema.displayMode` → retirement tombstone (`?: never`) with the JSDoc pointing at `type` as the replacement, citing discriminator prong 2 (advertised at `CHANGELOG.md:578`, 3.3.0) exactly as the ui seat's 02:32Z measurement at `5548764449` established.
- `packages/plugin-chatbot/src/renderer.tsx` — remove the `displayMode` entry from `chatbot-floating`'s `inputs` (the "Display Mode" control) and the `defaultProps.displayMode: 'floating'` seed. A control is restated, never deleted into a vacuum (#7070): the restatement is the tombstone plus the changeset text.
- Stored documents: `displayMode` is in the #6152 unmirrored ledger and `BaseSchema` is passthrough, so runtime validation of this key is unchanged (zero, before and after). The changeset must say so in one sentence, and the PR carries the same tripwire shape as #7669 so that minting a mirror under #6152 forces the `retirementTombstone()` half at that time.

Not taken: A (two spellings for one decision, and a behaviour change on a key that shipped inert); C (the published type keeps teaching an AI author a switch that does not exist).

**Execution**: `domain:ui` seat. Clause-② yes (public type member retired); `@object-ui/types` `minor` + BREAKING with the launch-window banner, `@object-ui/plugin-chatbot` `patch`. Contract review at tier is the ui seat's, in-seat, per the 2026-08-31 ownership ruling — director audits after the fact only. Once this PR merges the card has no open half and closes on it; a closing keyword is fine this time.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` stripped; `pm:queue`, `finding`, `domain:ui` retained. Ledger: objectstack director seat post #12708, summon #14.

## ⛔ The dispatch fence this PR was built on was STALE, and that is the seat's error, not the dev seat's

The contract review of PR #7705 (comment to follow on that PR) found it first. Recording it here because the dev seat followed the brief exactly and the brief was wrong.

### What happened

My claim comment and both dispatch briefs said `displayMode` was **"parked on a maintainer decision"** and told the dev to carry it across unchanged because objectui#7654 owned its fate.

**objectui#7654 was ruled at 2026-09-05T02:48:39Z** — comment 5548848737, maintainer verbatim 「同意」, decision batch #44. **Ruling B: retire `displayMode`** — `?: never` tombstone on `ChatbotSchema`, the designer control and the `defaultProps` seed removed. `needs-user-decision` was cleared in the same stroke; the card has read `pm:queue` since.

The first dispatch of this card was killed by a rate limit. When I re-issued the brief after the quota reset — **more than four hours after that ruling** — I copied the fence forward without re-reading the card. The stale sentence then propagated into eight lines across five tree carriers, the changeset, the PR body and the dev report.

### Why it is worse than an ordinary stale read

The ruling cites **this seat's own measurement** as its ground: *"citing discriminator prong 2 (advertised at `CHANGELOG.md:578`, 3.3.0) exactly as the ui seat's 02:32Z measurement at `5548764449` established."*

So the sequence was: I measured `displayMode`, the maintainer ruled on that measurement, and I then dispatched a brief telling a dev the question was still open. ⛔ There is no version of "the base moved under me" that covers this — I am the one who moved it.

### The rule this breaks is the one this seat has been enforcing all day

Every dispatch brief and every review brief issued today carries: **⛔ read the current state of every card and PR you name before writing a tense for it.** Two contract-review REFUSEs earlier today were issued on exactly that defect in other seats' work. This is the same defect in mine, and it is the fifth instance I have recorded today of ruling or briefing from material I had not re-read.

⭐ The instruction is not enough on its own. Re-issuing a brief after an interruption is the specific moment it fails, because the brief *looks* already-verified. Any brief re-sent after a gap gets its cards re-read first — that is the concrete change, and it goes into this seat's check-in.

### What this changes for PR #7705

Nothing about the ruled shape (one interface per registration stands, #6169). What changes:

- Every `displayMode` tense in the tree, the changeset and the PR body must read **ruled B**, not parked.
- `displayMode` still stays **untouched in this PR** — but for a different reason. Not "pending a decision": the decision exists and its execution is **#7654's own PR**, which must tombstone the member on `ChatbotSchema` and strip the control and the seed. This PR must leave that member executable for it.
- Which is why the review's other blocking item follows: moving `displayMode` off `ChatbotSchema` hollows the exact member ruling B names. Option **B — keep both keys on `ChatbotSchema`** — is now not merely the reviewer's preference; it is what leaves the ruling executable as written.

Remediation dispatched with the corrected fence.
